items.title: Altitude training paradigm
items.claim: Levine and Stray-Gundersen's 'live high, train low' studies (1997) argued for which protocol?

options.text: Live at altitude (around 2,500 m) to stimulate red-cell production, but train at low altitude to maintain workload
Live and train at sea level
Train only at altitudes above 5,000 m

items.reveal_title: Sleep high, train low to combine adaptation and intensity
items.reveal:
The protocol attempts to gain the haematological benefits of altitude exposure without losing training quality.

Subsequent research and commercial 'altitude tents' aim to replicate the stimulus at any geographical location.
items.why: Elite training innovations often emerge from blending physiology and pragmatic logistics.

items.title: Title IX participation increase
items.claim: Title IX of the US Education Amendments (1972) banned sex discrimination in federally funded education, including athletics. By 2018, what proportion of US high school athletes were girls compared with 1971?

options.text: Roughly 10x more (about 295,000 in 1971 versus over 3 million by the 2010s)

items.reveal:
National Federation of State High School Associations data show girls' high school athletic participation rising from around 295,000 in 1971-72 to over 3.4 million in 2018-19.

Funding and facility disparities persist; the legal framework changed participation faster than parity.
items.why: Single policy interventions can reshape participation across decades.

items.title: Biological passports
items.claim: WADA introduced the Athlete Biological Passport in 2009 to detect doping. What does it primarily monitor?

options.text: Longitudinal changes in biomarkers (e.g. haematological) that suggest manipulation, even without a positive substance test

items.reveal:
The passport tracks haematological, steroidal and (more recently) endocrine markers across an athlete's career. Significant deviations can trigger sanctions even without finding the substance itself.

The approach has produced sanctions where direct testing failed.
items.why: Indirect, statistical evidence has become a major tool in anti-doping enforcement.
